### P0. What the book really is (three corrections to the text above)
1. The ladder cell says mode = long (/mnt/l2/l2vast/_lon/ladder_cells.json, id L1acc170a, key Asia|kagi_20|trig_levels_vwap|false_break|{"M": 3, "k": 0.5}|sym15u|long), BUT the events file used by every P45 set is BOTH sides: brkt_build.build() (code/th_brkt/brkt_build.py:62-64) matches the book's own file with mode both when the long-only build does not match ("the old L-id of a one-side cell was built with both sides"). The 89 / 52 signals below are both sides and equal the events file exactly (89 of 89 and 52 of 52 entry seconds found in /mnt/l2/l2vast/_brkt/ev/L1acc170a_R0_P45.parquet).
2. Session clock: Asia = ET 18:00 to 02:00 (code/th_bars/common.py:13-16, code 0 for minute-of-day >= 1080 or < 120; trading date = ET + 6 h). On td 20261027 (EDT) the session opens 22:00Z, not 23:00Z; on td 20261110 (EST) 23:00Z. The 22:01Z signals of 20261027 are inside the session.
3. Stage-1 exit rows for this book are queued (see summary); this section is only the parity pack.

### P1. kagi_20 kernel: exact rules (code/th_bars/kernels.py:197-223 `k_dchg`; kagi_p is built by the same call as dchg_p: code/th_bars/build_month.py:127-128)
Units: prices are int ticks (0.25 pt) inside the kernel; load_bars multiplies o/h/l/c by 0.25 (code/th_grid/gjob.py:40). theta is in TICKS.
1. Reversal amount theta (ticks) = max(2, round(20 * s_rng(td))) (build_month.py:120 `rs`, 127-128 with p = 20; np.round = half-to-even), s_rng = trailing median of the daily range of the 20 stats_day rows before the td divided by r0 (build_month.py:13-22; same s_rng as in autopilot/D8_ASIA_NEWBOOK_INPUTS.md section 2). So 20 is a multiplier on the volatility scale, NOT 20 ticks and NOT percent. Values used here: td 20261027 s_rng 2.189948 -> theta 44 ticks (11.00 pt); td 20261110 s_rng 3.048303 -> theta 61 ticks (15.25 pt). Check: the smallest |c-o| of any stored bar of the day equals theta (44.0 and 61.0 ticks).
   GAP: theta varies by td; for a td without a stats_day row the code clamps to the last row (build_month.py:71 np.minimum); live s_rng must be produced the same way (trailing 20-row median, r0 = 191.5 pt, see D8_ASIA_NEWBOOK_INPUTS.md section 2 for the piecewise daily-range quirk).
2. State resets (no bar emitted, open leg dropped) at every change of session key (td*10+code) or instrument id (kernels.py:202).
3. First print of the session: st = ehi = elo = its price, t0 = te = its time, d = 0 (lines 204-205). Its volume counts (vol += sz is done BEFORE all tests, line 206).
4. Undecided phase (d == 0, lines 208-212): track ehi = max, elo = min of prints. If p - elo >= theta: UP leg, st = elo (the LOW of the undecided phase), ext = p. Else if ehi - p >= theta: DOWN leg, st = ehi, ext = p. Up is tested first.
5. UP leg (d == 1, lines 213-217): if p > ext (strictly): ext = p, te = ts. Else if ext - p >= theta (>=, only tested when the print is not a new extreme): reversal -> emit bar, then st = ext, d = -1, ext = p (the reversal print), counters reset, t0 = te = ts of the reversal print. DOWN leg symmetric (lines 218-222): p < ext new extreme; p - ext >= theta reverses.
6. Bar emitted once per COMPLETED leg, at the confirming print: UP leg o = st, h = ext, l = st, c = ext; DOWN leg o = st, h = st, l = ext, c = ext (lines 216 / 221). So o/h/l/c are the leg start and extreme PRINT PRICES (no tick rounding to a grid). A leg is therefore at least theta ticks (|c-o| >= theta), except nothing is dropped.
7. Next leg starts at st = previous extreme (not the reversal print); its ext starts at the reversal print price, so its first c may be closer than theta to its o (the leg is emitted only if it later reverses by theta from its own extreme; its |c-o| >= theta is not guaranteed by the first reversal print alone but holds for the stored bars checked, see 1).
8. Volume / n / dlt: sum over all prints from the leg's first print (after a reversal: from the print AFTER the reversal print) through the confirming print; the reversal print is added BEFORE the test (line 206) and the counters are reset AFTER emitting (line 217), so the reversal print's volume is in the OLD (emitted) bar and not the new one; dlt = sum(side*size). Bar volume of the first leg starts at the session's first print.
9. Time: _emit(..., t0, te, ts[i], ...) (lines 216/221): t0 = first print of the leg, t1 (te) = time of the extreme print, KNOWN time = ts[i] = the tape timestamp of the confirming (reversal) print. The stored t_close used by the signal code and the engine = known_ts (iface.py:8, gjob.py:40). The extreme time te is earlier than the known time (median lag 25-330 s per code/th_grid/gate_doc.py:58); the signal is stamped at the confirming print.
10. The open leg at session end is NOT emitted (no flush). Bars of the next leg can be emitted microseconds after the previous one when price runs: see bars 1 and 2 of 20261027 (known 22:01:12.091458 and 22:01:12.111152).
11. Print granularity: kagi is UNAFFECTED by the D8 print rule (autopilot/D8_PRINT_RULE.md table row kagi: 100.00% of run-merge bars equal the old-engine bars in O/H/L/C + close time, month 2026-10, 8 rows 147,066 bars). Bars below are the stored /mnt/l2/l2vast/_bars/kagi_20 bars read by the engine.
GAP: I did NOT rebuild the two days from raw tape here (no tape pass in the 25-minute window); the bars are the stored ones, which the engine used. gate_doc.py:48 records an independent causal replay of kagi_14 vs stored bars (20 of 20 sessions identical), not of kagi_20.

### P2. Trigger: trig_levels_vwap, variant false_break, params {"M": 3, "k": 0.5} (code/th_grid/triggers_d/lv_vwap.py:6-8; lv_base.py:19-43; fd_common.py:57-90 level_events, edge/shift/roll_any 40-56)
- Variant is the PLAIN one (not _native): unit u = 5.0 points FIXED (lv_base.py U0 = 5.0; _ev: `u=... else np.full(len, U0)`). So k = 0.5 means 0.5 * 5.0 = 2.5 points. M = 3 means within the last 3 bars (j-3..j-1) of the kagi_20 series.
- Lines (LINES, lv_vwap.py:8), tried in this order, first line that fires wins on a bar: VWAP0__V (session VWAP from 18:00 ET), RVWAP0__V (RTH 09:30 VWAP), LVWAP0__V (London 02:00 VWAP), YVWAP__V (prior-day VWAP), AVPDH__V (VWAP anchored at the prior-day high), AVPDL__V (anchored at prior-day low), WVWAP__V (weekly), MVWAP__V (monthly). They are 1-minute typical-price x volume VWAPs, stored as raw-price minute arrays /mnt/l2/l2vast/_bars/feat_d/lines/<name>.npy (fd_common.py:7,17-20). GAP: the builder of those arrays (fd_levels.py) was not read; INPUTS below gives the values the engine used so the relay can compare.
- Level value used for bar j: the line at the last minute START <= T0_j, stale <= 120 s (fd_common.py:27-40, line_index/line_at); T0_j = max(t_close[j-1], t_open[j]) capped at t_close[j] (decision_s); these bars have no t_open, so T0_j = known time of bar j-1 (bar 0: NaN at the session start, no signal). The minute entry i uses minutes < i only. Lines can be NaN (e.g. VWAP0 right at the open): NaN = no signal from that line.
- Logic per line L, bar j with closes c: up = c > L + k*u; dn = c < L - k*u. roll_any(up, M) = up was true on any of bars j-M..j-1. SHORT (fade of a failed upside break) = roll_any(up, 3) and c[j] < L (c[j] strictly below the line, no k margin). LONG = roll_any(dn, 3) and c[j] > L. Event = rising edge (edge(): true now and not true on the previous bar). A bar with both a long and a short firing (from different lines) is dropped (fd_common.py:114-115). The signal stamp = t_close of bar j = known time; entry = that time + 2 s (market through the engine, ts = sig_ts // 1e9 + 2, brkt_build.py:41).
- Session filter: bar in Asia session (sess_id % 10 == 0) and part == 0 (brkt_build.py:36-38).
- Observation: AVPDH__V (anchored VWAP of the prior-day high) sits within a few points of the very first bars' prices on both days, so the first ~30 signals of 20261027 are price oscillating around that line (fired_line column).

### P3. Bracket and position rule
- P45 = fixed stop 45.0 pt / target 45.0 pt on every entry (brkt_build.py:15 SHAPES P45; events columns stop_pts = tgt_pts = 45). Entry = market at +2 s after the known time; exit = whichever of stop / target is hit, else the session end exit_ts (02:00 ET) with the 120 s tape cap (cap_exit.cap_events); realized in the engine as Target / Stop / UWTime (see TRADES).
- One position at a time: evidence = engine run TL3_ALN_AS_L1acc170a_R0BRP45 (month 202610): 130 trades, 0 overlapping (entry before the previous exit: 0); on 20261027, 89 signals produce 14 trades; a signal arriving while a position is open is skipped, the first signal after the exit that is not skipped starts the next trade (see TRADES vs SIGNALS column taken_by_engine). GAP: I did not find the line of code in mf_multi.py (outside this window) that enforces it; the rule is read from the output. Two opposite signals in the same second (bars 1 and 2 on 20261027) -> the first (-1) is taken.

### P4. Blocks for td 20261027 and 20261110
BARS = stored kagi_20 Asia bars (part 0). SIGNALS = trig_levels_vwap false_break output on those bars, both sides, with the line that fired and its value. INPUTS = per bar: T0 (decision time) and the 8 line values at T0 (empty = NaN). 20261027: 196 bars, 89 signals; 20261110: 131 bars, 52 signals. TRADES: 20261027 from the engine set TL3_ALN_AS_L1acc170a_R0BRP45 (1 lot, bare); 20261110 NOT LANDED (engine month 202611 does not exist in any runs tree; no values invented).
